questions.question: How many countries were evaluated in the Climate Change Performance Index 2025?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI) evaluates **63 countries** responsible for over 90% of global greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• The CCPI is published annually by **Germanwatch, NewClimate Institute, and Climate Action Network International**.
 
• It assesses countries based on **four categories**: Greenhouse Gas Emissions, Renewable Energy, Energy Use, and Climate Policy.
 
• The index is designed to highlight efforts and gaps in combating climate change among the world's major emitters.
 
• The CCPI aims to increase transparency in international climate politics and serves as a tool to press governments into enhancing climate action.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The CCPI uses a scoring system where countries are ranked on their performance in mitigating climate change, with high performers categorized as "Very High" and low performers as "Very Low."
 
• The CCPI includes indicators such as the **Paris Agreement targets** to evaluate countries' progress toward limiting global warming to below 2°C.
 
• The index is widely recognized as an independent monitoring tool that holds countries accountable for their climate commitments.
 
• Top-performing countries often include **Scandinavian nations** due to their strong climate policies and renewable energy adoption.
 
• Countries like **Saudi Arabia, Russia, and Iran** typically rank low due to insufficient climate action and high fossil fuel dependency.

questions.question: The Rural Landless Labour Employment Guarantee Programme (RLEGP) was started in which of the following Five-Year Plans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sixth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sixth Five-Year Plans**

 
 
• In **October 1980**, then-prime minister** Indira Gandhi **reorganised and rebranded the** Food For Work Program as the National Rural Employment Program.**
 
• As of **April 1981**, it became a **regular programme.**
 
• The** Sixth Five Year Plan** saw the beginning of the **Program**. It tries to implement more **employment **for those who are **underemployed**.
 
• The Rural Landless Employment Guarantee was a central government-funded programme that provided landless people with work guarantees for at least 100 days.
 
• 10% of the money was also set aside for the sole benefit of SC/ST communities, with the remaining 25% going to social forestry and the remaining 20% to housing.
 
• On **April 1, 1989, Rajiv Gandhi**, the prime minister, merged the **Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Program** and the **National Rural Employment Program** to create the **Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (JRY). **
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• ** Seventh Five-Year Plans**

 
 
• ​In 1985, when **Rajiv Gandhi** led the Congress party to power, the** seventh five-year plan** was unveiled. The seventh planet's time period spanned from 1 April 1985 to 31 March 1990.
 
• From 1985 to 1987, **Mr Manmohan Singh** served as the **Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission.** Food, work, and production were the first three plans included in the **seventh strategy.**
 
 
 
• **Fifth Five-Year Plans**
 
 
• ​The government of **Indira Gandhi **created **India's Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974–1979).**
 
• It put an emphasis on agriculture, reducing poverty, and creating jobs.
 
• Additionally, the plan attempted to lessen social and economic disparities within society.
 
 
 
• **Fourth** Five-Year Plans
 
 
• ​The** Fourth Five-Year Plan** embraced the goal of reversing the prior trend of greater economic and wealth power concentration.
 
• It was based on the Gadgil formula, which put an emphasis on growth while maintaining stability and moving towards **independence**.
 
• **Indira Gandhi **was in office as prime minister at the time.

questions.question: As per the World Bank report, by how much percentage did extreme poverty in India fall between 2011-12 and 2022-23?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**from 16.2% to 2.3%.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **According to the World Bank's Poverty & Equity Brief, extreme poverty in India fell from 16.2% in 2011-12 to 2.3% in 2022-23.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **171 million people were lifted out of extreme poverty during this period.**
 
• **Rural extreme poverty dropped from 18.4% to 2.8%, while urban poverty declined from 10.7% to 1.1%.**
 
• India transitioned into the lower-middle-income category using the $3.65 per day poverty line.
 
• States like Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar, West Bengal, and Madhya Pradesh contributed significantly to the decline.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Extreme Poverty Line**__: Defined by the World Bank as living on less than $2.15 per day (PPP terms).
 
• __**Lower-Middle-Income Category (LMIC)**__: Refers to countries with GNI per capita between $1,036 and $4,045 according to World Bank classification.
 
• __**Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)**__: Measures non-monetary aspects of poverty like health, education, and living standards, declined to 16.4% by 2019-21.
 
• __**Employment Trends**__: Recent trends show rising employment rates, especially among women, and urban unemployment falling to 6.6% in early FY24/25.

questions.question: The constitutional provision Center-State relationship has been borrowed from which of the following countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Canada**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Center-State relationship** in India has been influenced by the federal model of **Canada**. The Indian Constitution adopted the **concept of a strong central government** with specific powers allocated to the states, similar to Canada's structure.
 
• The **Canadian Constitution** provides for a federal system where powers are divided between the central and provincial governments. However, the central government retains significant power, making it a **quasi-federal structure**.
 
• In India, the division of powers between the **Union** and the **States** is specified in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution, which includes three lists: the Union List, the State List, and the Concurrent List.
 
• The principle of **residuary powers** (powers not enumerated in the Constitution) lies with the central government in India, similar to Canada's system. This is outlined in **Article 248** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Canadian model also influenced the concept of an **appointed governor** for provinces by the central government, which is similar to the appointment of governors in Indian states by the President.
 
• While Canada inspired the Center-State relationship, India's federal structure has unique features, including a three-tier system (Union, State, and Local levels) and greater emphasis on unitary principles during emergencies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Center-State Relationship in India:**

 
 
• The Indian Constitution divides responsibilities between the **Union** and the **States** through the **Union List**, **State List**, and **Concurrent List**. The Union List includes subjects of national importance like defense, while the State List includes subjects like police and public health.
 
• In case of a conflict between the Union and State laws on a subject in the Concurrent List, the **Union law prevails**, ensuring a stronger central authority.
 
 
 
• **Features of Canadian Federalism:**
 
 
• **Canada** follows a **quasi-federal structure**, with significant powers concentrated in the central government while provinces enjoy autonomy in specific areas.
 
• The **residuary powers** lie with the central government in Canada, similar to India's framework, where unmentioned subjects are allocated to the Union Government.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Federal Models:**
 
 
• Unlike the **USA**, where states enjoy more autonomy, or **Germany**, which emphasizes cooperative federalism, India's federal structure leans towards **centralization** like Canada.
 
• The **Australian model** of federalism, by contrast, divides powers between the central and state governments more equitably.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Constitutional Provisions:**

 
 
• **Articles 245-263** of the Indian Constitution detail the Center-State legislative, administrative, and financial relations.
 
• The **Finance Commission**, established under **Article 280**, ensures equitable financial distribution between the Union and the States.
 
 
 
• **Significant Influences:**
 
 
• The **Government of India Act, 1935**, laid the foundation for India's federal structure by introducing provincial autonomy, further refined in the Constitution.
 
• During emergencies under **Articles 352, 356, and 360**, India's federal structure becomes more unitary, a feature absent in Canada's federal framework.

questions.question: In 1887, the Royal Society, London gave the Davy Medal for the ‘discovery of the periodic law of chemical elements’ to _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**John Alexander Newland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1887, the Royal Society, London** gave the **Davy Medal **for the **‘discovery of the periodic law of chemical elements’ **to **John Alexander Newland**.
 
• British chemist, **John Alexander Reina Newlands** specialised in **elemental periodicity**.
 
• **John Newlands **was the first to create a **table of chemical elements grouped according to their respective atomic weight**.
 
• He made his idea of the **periodicity of the chemical elements**, which he had arranged in order of atomic weight, public in** 1864**.
 
• In order to make a **connection with musical octaves**, Newlands named this phenomenon,** The Law of Octaves** after noticing **commonalities between elements whose atomic weights varied by seven**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The first person to arrange chemical elements according to their atomic weights was** AEB de Chancourtois**, who also created an **early version of the periodic table known as the "telluric helix" because tellurium was in the centre**.
 
• Russian chemist and inventor **Dmitri Ivanovich Mendeleev** is best known for conceiving th**e Periodic Law and developing a preliminary version of the periodic table of elements**.
 
• A pioneer in creating the** first iterations of the periodic table of chemical elements** was the German chemist **Julius Lothar Meyer**.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution deals with the session, prorogation and dissolution of the Parliament?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Article ****85**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Article 85** of the Indian Constitution addresses parliamentary sessions, prorogations, and dissolutions.

__
 
• **The President **may call **sessions of each House of Parliamen**t at any time and location, but no more than **six months** may pass between the last meeting of one session and the date set for the first meeting of the following session. 
 
• The President has the authority to **dissolve** the House of People and **prorogue** both Houses from time to time.
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

A **session** is the **time frame** in which the House convenes to transact business. According to the Indian Constitution, the President may call joint sessions of both Houses of Parliament no more frequently than every six months.

Typically, *there are three sessions per year*. There will be many meetings during a session.

 
• The sessions often consist of the following:
 
 
• Budget meeting (February to May)
 
• The monsoon session (July to September)
 
• Winter session (November to December)
 
 

***The Lok Sabha is dissolved either automatically at the end of its five-year term or by executive action.*** The life of the house comes to an end at dissolution.

 
• **The Rajya Sabha remains in place.**

 
 
• A third of its members are up for election every two years, and its members serve fixed terms of six years.
 
 

**Prorogation denotes the conclusion of a meeting.** Prorogation signifies that both the sitting and the session are over, not that the House has been dissolved.

 
• While the House is in session, the President may also prorogue it.
 
• A few days after the House is adjourned sine die by the House presiding officer, the President often publishes a notice for the prorogation of the session.
 
• Following the prorogation of the House, all outstanding notices expire.
 
• *Bills, however, are unaffected by prorogation.*
 
• **Recess** is the *period of time between prorogation and reassembly.*

questions.question: Which is the article that deals with the official language ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 343**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 343 of the Indian Constitution** declares **Hindi as the official language** of India.
 
• However, it also allows for the use of English as an official language until a resolution is passed by the Parliament to replace it with Hindi.
 
• Hindi is one of the 22 scheduled languages of India.
 
• The Constitution also recognizes the importance of preserving and promoting the rich linguistic and cultural diversity of the country.
 
• Apart from Hindi and English, many other languages are used for official purposes in different states and Union Territories of India.
 
• The Constitution also provides for the development of Hindi as a link language for the whole of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Article 88
 
 
• Article 88 deals with the rights of Ministers and the Attorney-General of India to speak and participate in the proceedings of either House of Parliament or any of its committees, though they are not entitled to vote.
 
 
 
• Article 123
 
 
• Article 123 of the Indian Constitution deals with the power of the President to promulgate ordinances during the recess of Parliament.
 
• It does not deal with the official language of India.
 
 
 
• Article 301
 
 
• Article 301 of the Indian Constitution deals with the freedom of trade, commerce, and intercourse throughout India.
 
• It does not deal with the official language of India.

questions.question: In which of the following festival of Kerala, Lord Vishnu and his incarnation Lord Krishna are honoured?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Vishu__.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****

__
 
• **Vishu** is a **Hindu festival** observed in **Kerala, Mangalore, Karnataka's Udupi region,** Pondicherry's Mahé district, and certain neighbouring districts of Tamil Nadu, as well as its diaspora groups.
 
• The celebration begins on the first day of Medam, Kerala's ninth lunar month.
 
• As a result, 14 or 15 April in the Gregorian calendar, always falls in the middle of April. I
 
• It has something to do with April's harvest.
 
• Because Lord Vishnu is regarded as the God of Time, Lord Vishnu and his incarnation Lord Krishna are honoured on Vishu.** **

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the new Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in September 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shirish Chandra Murmu.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Shirish Chandra Murmu has been appointed as the Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), effective October 9, 2025.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shirish Chandra Murmu will serve a three-year tenure as Deputy Governor of RBI, succeeding Rajeshwar Rao.**
 
• **Murmu is currently serving as Executive Director at RBI and has extensive experience in banking supervision and financial policy formulation.**
 
• **The role of the Deputy Governor includes overseeing key areas like monetary policy, financial markets regulation, and banking supervision.**
 
• **Murmu’s appointment ensures continuity and strengthens RBI’s leadership team amidst ongoing economic challenges.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Role of RBI Deputy Governor__

 __
 
• RBI Deputy Governors oversee critical areas such as monetary policy, financial regulation, banking supervision, and other regulatory functions.
 
 
 
• Leadership Transition__
 __
 
• Murmu will replace Rajeshwar Rao, continuing the policy work in banking regulation and supervision at RBI.
 
 
 
• RBI’s Focus Areas__
 
 
• The RBI is focused on enhancing financial stability, improving governance in banks, and supporting India’s economic growth.
